item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Retailgentic: AI Is a New Customer Category: Wharton Professor & Bodhium Labs Co-Founder Kartik Hosanagar
item.content:encoded:
Score: 100/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

This episode features a Wharton professor and founder discussing agentic commerce, AI as a customer, and eCommerce funnel transformation. The strategic insights, frameworks (levels of agentic commerce), and real-world examples (protocol wars, digital twins) are highly relevant for a principal PM moving to director. Guest authority and actionable takeaways are strong, and the episode is dense with strategic ideas.

Summary

Kartik Hosanagar, Wharton professor and Bodhium Labs co-founder, explores the emergence of AI as a new customer category in commerce. The conversation covers agentic commerce levels, parallels to autonomous vehicles, and how AI is fundamentally transforming brand discovery and the consideration funnel. Kartik shares actionable strategies for brands to adapt to these changes, discusses protocol wars between Google, OpenAI, and Amazon, and explains Bodhium's work in simulating AI search behaviors. The episode delivers concrete frameworks and strategic guidance for product leaders navigating AI-driven retail transformation.

Key Ideas

  • AI is becoming a distinct customer category, requiring new strategies for persuasion and engagement.
  • Agentic commerce has levels of autonomy, fundamentally changing discovery and consideration in eCommerce.
  • Protocol wars (UCP vs ACP) and digital twin simulations are reshaping how brands interact with AI-driven platforms.

Implications

Product leaders must rethink customer acquisition and funnel strategies as AI intermediates discovery and purchase decisions. Understanding protocol dynamics and simulation tools will be critical for competitive advantage in agentic commerce.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #3 — The SaaS Podcast: Stuck at $50K ARR for 5 Years. Now $1.5M With AI Agents.
item.content:encoded:
Score: 73/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

This episode delivers a concrete founder/operator case study with direct lessons on SaaS growth, AI agent deployment, and channel economics. The guest is a hands-on operator with relevant experience, and the content is actionable for product leaders focused on AI and business strategy.

Summary

George Georgiadis, founder of Happier Leads, shares his journey from a stagnant $50K ARR to $1.5M ARR by leveraging AI agents and strategic channel ownership. He details the transition from a point tool to a full platform, the importance of owning infrastructure (mailboxes, data), and the use of AI to automate support and bug fixing. The episode provides actionable insights on product strategy, channel economics, and the operational impact of AI in SaaS. It offers a rare, detailed look at bootstrapping, scaling, and making strategic decisions in a competitive market.

Key Ideas

  • AI agents as a lever for scaling SaaS with minimal headcount
  • Owning channel infrastructure to reduce costs and increase control
  • Strategic platform expansion as a competitive moat

Implications

Product leaders can extract lessons on leveraging AI for operational efficiency, channel strategy, and platform differentiation. The episode is highly relevant for those building or scaling AI-driven SaaS products.

Summary

The episode examines how AI can be used as a 'thinking partner' rather than a source of definitive answers, especially in contexts of workplace communication and emotional management. Guest 'Waki' shares his transition from TSMC manager to creator, offering practical demonstrations of AI-powered conversation training for boundary-setting and emotional regulation. While the episode touches on the use of AI for workflow and decision support, the focus remains on interpersonal skills and psychological safety, with only moderate relevance to product strategy or AI technology leadership.

Key Ideas

  • AI as a thinking partner for structured decision-making.
  • Practical demonstration of AI-assisted conversation training.
  • Building external systems for emotional regulation and boundary-setting.

Implications

Some transferable lessons for using AI in workflow and decision support, but limited strategic or business case analysis.
